note.en: Bengali tradition places the Virata pitha at the Vidyeshwari (Ambika) shrine here.

history.en: Green Message identifies Virata with Viratnagar (Bairat) in the Jaipur district of Rajasthan, the ancient Viratanagara that was capital of the Iron Age Matsya kingdom. Bengali tradition instead names the Vidyeshwari (Ambika) shrine at Patiram in the Dakshin Dinajpur district of West Bengal. Neither shrine has been located on a map, so both pins mark the towns.

story.en: According to the Puranas, Sati, the daughter of Daksha, gave up her life in the fire of her father's sacrifice after he insulted her husband Shiva. Grieving, Shiva carried her body across the world until Vishnu's discus divided it, and each place where a part fell became a Shakti Peetha. Tradition holds that Sati's toes of the left foot fell here.

en: Bairat corresponds to Viratanagara, capital of the ancient Matsya kingdom.
The ruins of the Bijak-ki-pahadi at Bairat, a Buddhist chaitya of the 3rd century BCE, are the oldest free-standing Buddhist structures in India.
Two rock edicts of the emperor Ashoka were found at Bairat.
Banglapedia names Virata among the eight famous pithas of West Bengal in the Mahapithanirupana.

timings.en: No official timings are published; check locally before visiting.
